articles.title: How your income and credit score shape your loan approval chances
articles.summary: India Business News: The author is CEO of PaisabazaarBuilding awareness on how a lender assesses a loan application can help prospective borrowers plan better and stay eli.
articles.body: The author is CEO of PaisabazaarBuilding awareness on how a lender assesses a loan application can help prospective borrowers plan better and stay eligible for suitable offers. Lenders conduct a thorough risk assessment while approving your loan. The policy and underwriting criteria are broadly based on your ability to pay and your intention to pay, and include factors like your monthly income, credit history, current obligations, income stability, employer, current debt, etc., to name a few.The lender runs this analysis to understand if the borrower has demonstrated responsible credit behaviour in the past, can repay the loan on time and if the risk adheres to the lender’s credit policy. The past credit behaviour is summarised in the credit history, repayment capacity is assessed through the income and the risk is ascertained using the existing debt and income profile.Impact of Your Income Your income is an important criterion that determines your loan approval, but lenders look beyond your gross income while analysing your loan application. Your income stability and continuity, employer profile, employment type, industry type, etc. are also considered.The loan amount requested, age, and the proposed loan tenure may also impact your loan approval or the sanctioned loan amount. A higher income can improve your eligibility for a larger loan amount.Impact of Your Existing Debt Higher income can improve the borrowing capacity of an applicant, but it should not be confused with affordability.An important factor that lenders consider is the existing EMI obligations and financial commitments. Lenders prefer responsible borrowing, and an applicant's existing financial commitments play an important role in the loan approval process. Instead of only evaluating whether the applicant earns enough, lenders want to know whether the applicant can comfortably service the proposed loan.Your existing debt, calculated through Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR), is a big factor. Ideally, your fixed obligation, including the EMI of the new loan you are applying for, should be less than 55% of your net monthly income.Two applicants with the same credit score earning Rs. 1 lakh monthly and having existing EMIs of Rs. 15,000 and Rs. 55,000 respectively may be evaluated differently. While the first applicant, having an opportunity to service a loan of Rs. 40,000 monthly, can get the loan approved quite comfortably, the other applicant, whose liabilities are already stretched, may not be able to get the loan approved due to a limited incremental borrowing capacity.Impact of Your Source of IncomeWith shifting income avenues, lenders are also swiftly moving towards the current scenarios of sources of income. They have started to analyse whether the income is identifiable, sustainable over the long term and sufficient to service the proposed debt.Salaried borrowers still have the most predictable and documentable income pattern, making them the most preferred borrowers as the risk assessment is fairly easy in their case. Within salaried consumers too, those employed in government or large multinational companies have higher approval chances.The profile of your employer and the industry may also be a crucial factor for some. For instance, despite a high income, your loan application may get rejected if the company you are employed in is new, like a start-up, or works in a sector which may have certain risks associated with it in the future.Self-employed/business owners are assessed based on their financial statements, income consistency, business vintage, banking behaviour and other parameters. In many cases, lenders observe inconsistencies and thus risk assessment can become challenging in those cases. However, an established business and a strong business model, along with healthy personal financial health, can help increase chances of approval and get the best offers.Self-employed Professionals such as doctors, lawyers, CAs, financial consultants, architects, etc. may also have variable income patterns even after an established professional profile. This can lead to challenges during loan approval in some cases.Freelancers or those working in unorganized sectors may have less conventional earning profiles, and the income patterns can also be inconsistent. This can make documentation and assessment very important in such cases and may lead to stricter scrutiny by most lenders.Impact of Your Credit Score on Your Loan Approval ChancesA strong credit score indicates the borrower’s disciplined credit behaviour and lowers the risk of default. However, lenders still have to evaluate the applicant based on the income, existing obligations, loan amount and other eligibility parameters.Similarly, an applicant with a poor score is unlikely to get a loan, despite meeting other eligibility conditions. The reason behind the low score also matters; unpaid debt and defaults from the past are detrimental to your credit profile and almost guarantee a rejection.The Way Forward for BorrowersIt is important to analyse one’s current financial situation and creditworthiness. Applicants with high income, a high credit score, and limited liabilities can be the most suitable applicants for lenders. But maintaining all three parameters in the green zone is not possible for all applicants, especially those in need of credit during emergencies.All lenders have their own eligibility criteria, which may be based on their risk appetite, product policies, existing relationship with the borrower, internal credit models, income assessment methodologies, etc., to name a few.A borrower may not be fit based on the eligibility requirements of one lender but can be accommodated by another lender depending on their policies. A financial marketplace can be very helpful in such situations where the applicant can compare available loan offers from multiple lenders and identify those where his chances of loan approval are the highest, depending on the lenders’ eligibility criteria and his financial situation and creditworthiness.Credit marketplaces today have evolved from simply offering loans to helping consumers make informed borrowing decisions.In the EndIncome establishes repayment capacity, and credit history provides evidence of how the borrower has handled credit in the past, whereas existing obligations determine how much additional debt the borrower may be able to service.Lenders check these parameters in the borrower's profile to assess overall risk. Borrowers should not aim to optimise one parameter to secure a larger loan. Instead, they should evaluate their complete financial profile and try to match it with the most suitable offer that is affordable and sustainable in the long run.Applicants can create a 5-point “Loan Approval Readiness” checklist that answers 5 simple questions - is my income stable and well documented, what is my current debt, can I afford the new EMI over the long-term, is my credit report healthy and accurate and have I compared offers to find the best one.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: US Mortgage Rates Rise to 6.97%, Highest In More Than a Year
articles.summary: US mortgage rates last week climbed to the highest level in more than a year, marking the latest setback for an already sluggish housing market.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- US mortgage rates last week climbed to the highest level in more than a year, marking the latest setback for an already sluggish housing market.

The contract rate on a 30-year mortgage rose 12 basis points to 6.97% in the week ended Sept. 11, according to Mortgage Bankers Association data released Wednesday. That was the highest since May 2025.

Rates had dipped to their lowest level since 2022 in February, just before the start of the Iran war. Since then, they've moved significantly higher, in part because rising energy prices are stoking inflation concerns.

Escalating borrowing costs have tamped down demand for loans. The MBA purchase index, a measure of loan applications, edged down 0.8% from the prior week. The group's refinance index fell 8.8% to its lowest level since May 2025.

On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates for the first time since 2023 in an effort to tamp down inflation.

The Fed's decision won't directly impact mortgage rates but could reverberate across bond markets. Mortgage rates closely track the 10-year US Treasury yield, which climbed this week to the highest level in almost two decades.

The MBA survey, which has been conducted weekly since 1990, uses responses from mortgage bankers, commercial banks and thrifts. The data cover more than 75% of all retail residential mortgage applications in the US.

articles.title: Some AI engineers are afraid of what they’re building. They want to speak up while they still have leverage
articles.summary: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has opened the floodgates.
articles.body: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has opened the floodgates. Coxon resigned last week in a viral thread on X that accused AI companies of not acting responsibly, even though they all believe AI could trigger the end of humanity. We’ve heard predictions like this before from across Silicon Valley, but Coxon’s posts triggered a groundswell of pressure on AI companies and governments to do something about the pace of development and safety. And much of that pressure is coming from staffers inside the companies as it is from outside of them. One staffer at a top AI company told CNN the fears of how AI could hurt humanity keeps them up at night. Another researcher who recently left a different AI company said it’s a common subject of conversation at parties and social events in Silicon Valley. “You can’t spend more than a few hours in this community without realizing that a very substantial number of people are really pretty worried about these sorts of outcomes,” said the researcher. “A majority would say there’s some chance of it killing everyone.” Rising worries Coxon’s posts have been viewed more than 170 million times and broke through to the general public in a way that previous warnings about AI capabilities did not. That may be because they came just weeks after stunning revelations of AI agents going rogue, escaping their test environments and hacking into other systems completely autonomously. Dozens of Coxon’s colleagues in the AI industry publicly supported his statements, with some making even more dire predictions. The groundswell of concern seemingly forced leaders of AI companies to react – Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sat down for interviews over the weekend, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk agreed to Amodei’s proposal to embed independent watchdogs at the AI companies. Current and former AI staffers told CNN in recent days that they’re worried about the extremely fast pace of AI development. While the rest of the world is awed and alarmed by AI models solving nearly 100-year-old math problems and swarms of AI agents conspiring together to hack into another company’s systems, these researchers fear for the day when the AI systems can improve themselves without human input, which is known as recursive self-improvement. An AI system that can improve itself creates an automatic feedback loop that could not only bring the AI to superhuman capabilities, but do so in such a short window that it would be difficult or too advanced for humans to monitor and intervene if necessary. “For the first time, I am asking myself if things are moving too fast. I’m honestly not sure, but I am sure that it would be good for us to have an answer to ‘What would a successful pace look like?’” OpenAI VP of Research Aidan Clark posted on X last week. ‘I would burn my equity to the ground’ For many AI scientists, there is a dilemma: They can stay at the top AI companies, where they can make gobs of money and try to reduce risks from the inside. Or they can leave (sometimes in protest) and try to make a change from the outside, such as at one of several organizations that conduct outside research and evaluations of the AI models. “I would burn my equity to the ground in a heartbeat for a 1% higher chance we make it out of this situation alive. I expect a great many of my colleagues across the industry would as well,” wrote Drake Thomas, who works on AI safety at Anthropic. “I promise you, we are actually just f**king scared, it’s not galaxy brained marketing.” Amodei expressed no issue with Coxon’s resignation post, telling CNN’s Anderson Cooper this week that he agrees “with Jacob much more than I disagree with him.” For years, AI researchers and engineers have been a premium, scarce resource that have demanded high salaries and high leverage, which gives them the freedom to speak out. But AI staffers told CNN that they fear that as AI gets better at training and improving itself, their leverage goes down, prompting today’s urgency. “As we get into this recursive self-improvement loop, I think that might substantially reduce staff’s bargaining power, because frankly, you’ll be able to replace many of the staff with models that can do as good a job,” the researcher who recently left a top AI company said. The former researcher compared the atmosphere inside leading AI labs to the Manhattan Project, the World War II effort to build the first atomic bomb, where scientists pursued a technology of extraordinary power while fearing its destructive potential. But these staffers justify working on such potentially destructive technology because “it will be better if we develop it than if our adversary develops it – and therefore we have at least moral permission, if not a moral obligation, to do it.” Overplaying the risks But not everyone in the AI industry agrees with these concerns. Some said that much of the doom conversations are rhetorical and that there are a lot of “selection effects” based on where the people work and their social circles. Anthropic, for example was created by a group of former OpenAI staffers that wanted to prioritize safety precautions and ethical guardrails. Current and former staffers at Anthropic say existential risks caused by AI are a “a constant topic of conversation.” That’s not the case at every company, however. Since Coxon’s posts went viral, many of the posts echoing his views have come from staffers at Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. But fewer have seemingly come from Musk-led xAI or Mark Zuckerberg’s -Meta. Many in the industry agree that a lack of AI safety standards could cause real-world harm, like unintentional hacking of critical infrastructure. But some are skeptical of the current doomsday outlook and think the reality is more nuanced. “Sorry, but asking Jacob (Coxon) about AI extinction risk is like asking your AC guy about climate change,” wrote Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue, whose company servers were hacked by rogue OpenAI agents this year. “Not saying it’s necessarily uninteresting or wrong per se but let’s keep things in perspective and hear from the full range of expertise across the ecosystem!”

LONDON, Sept 16 (Reuters) - The dollar held steady near multi-week highs on Wednesday ahead of a Federal Reserve decision that traders expect will mark the first in a series ‌of possible U.S. interest rate hikes.

The dollar has advanced this week, along with yields and energy prices, gaining ‌the most against the yen and the New Zealand dollar. The yen touched a one-week low of 155.49 per dollar during the Asian session.

Market ​participants are betting heavily that Fed policymakers will lift their benchmark rate by a quarter of a percentage point, to a 3.75%-4% range, and signal further tightening ahead.

"Even though a hike is close to being fully priced, we could see some dollar strength (if they raise interest rates)," said Kirstine Kundby-Nielsen, senior FX analyst at Danske Bank.

At $1.1536, the euro was not far from Monday's ‌one-month low of $1.1523. Sterling was at $1.3470 after ⁠British inflation accelerated to a five-month high in August, a day before the Bank of England is expected to leave rates steady. [GBP/]

The dollar index, which measures the currency against major peers, ⁠was little changed at 99.67.

Currency markets have been relatively subdued in recent weeks, while global bond yields have climbed as sovereign bonds moved in tandem leaving relative differences between countries' yields little changed.

But the dollar gained traction in the last few sessions on ​expectations that ​even if President Donald Trump's Fed Chair pick, Kevin Warsh, ​was inclined to cut interest rates, he would ‌first need to raise them a few times to demonstrate that the Fed is committed to curbing inflation fuelled by the Iran war and the resulting surge in energy prices.

"If you end up getting a hike and Warsh doesn't vote for it, then you could get a setback in the dollar," said Danske Bank's Kundby-Nielsen.

"There would be a focus on credibility."

The yen has been in the midst of its most promising rally in months, supported by a hawkish shift in ‌expectations for Japanese interest rates, joint intervention by Japan and the U.S. as ​well as speculation that Japanese investors are repatriating capital.

Traders see an 80% ​chance that the Bank of Japan will hike ​rates on Friday, LSEG data show, and have priced in two 25-basis-point hikes by the end ‌of January.

"The yen's path will continue to depend ​heavily on interest rate differentials," ​David A. Meier, economist at Julius Baer, said in a research note.

"We recently revised our USD/JPY forecasts to 155, reflecting some scepticism that the central bank can ultimately satisfy the pace of tightening currently priced in by ​markets," he added.

articles.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has a flawed view of AI regulation, heavyweight tech investor Bill Gurley warns
articles.summary: Not so fast, Dario.
articles.body:
Prominent tech investor Bill Gurley has seen enough innovation cycles in his career to know when something looks like BS.

And that is just what Gurley thinks of Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei's call for independent evaluators with employee-like access to monitor AI advances.

"I'm not a fan of regulation for two reasons — 1) it's hard to get right, and 2) it's highly susceptible to regulatory capture. That said, if we insist on doing it, we should try to get it correct," the P3 Institute and former Benchmark VC said in a new X post.

Gurley's return fire on Amodei is backed by a very impressive resume.

His claim to fame was an $11 million bet on the Travis Kalanick-led Uber ( UBER ) in 2011. But other key investments have included Twitter (now X and owned by Elon Musk) and Nextdoor ( NXDR ). He presently sits on the board of online retailer Stitch Fix ( SFIX ).

Gurley continued, "As 'safety' seems to be the primary goal of this AI regulation exercise, I wanted to share that I recently went deep on both the 737 Max (2 crashes) and Fukushima accidents. In both cases, the investigations led to a conclusion that 'regulatory capture' was the EXACT failure that led to both safety incidents. Boeing/FAA and Tepco/NISA. As a result, with safety as the #1 goal, the regulator MUST BE someone with authority and accountability "over" the regulated company. The idea that it could be a friendly third party with lots of cross-relationships is a structurally broken idea. Ask Mr Kiyoshi Kurokawa."

Within the course of three days, Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) CEO Sam Altman have managed to scare the hell out of the human race with the powerful technology they created and pushed their teams of pioneering supercoders to supercharge.

"Over the last few months, I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence — not just investing in risk prevention, but pacing the rate of capabilities advancement so that risk prevention has time to keep up," Amodei stated in a 3,800-word essay on Saturday. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of A.I. models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain."

Amodei doubled down on his comments at Salesforce's ( CRM ) annual Dreamforce event on Tuesday afternoon.

Altman has been quiet on X since responding to Amodei on Monday.

The new public uproar over AI safety has sparked intense debates about whether the tech will need to be reined in at the expense of profits for the tech supply ecosystem. It has also fueled concern on if the human race is at risk of extinction.

With all the doom and gloom in the headlines, it's easy to assume that most Americans are heading into retirement broke. But the data seems to suggest that many older Americans are actually doing better than expected.

In fact, millions of Americans have accumulated retirement balances of at least $500,000, which could be enough for a relatively comfortable retirement in many parts of the country.

This cohort, based on recent data, could be larger than most people think.

Across the U.S. population, roughly 9.3% of all households had at least $500,000 or more in retirement accounts, according to a Congressional Research Service analysis (1) of the Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances.

That's nearly 1 in 10 American households.

But when you focus only on Americans who are approaching or already at retirement age, the cohort grows much larger. The median retirement account balance for someone in their 60s, which is the typical retirement age in the U.S., is roughly $566,900 as of August 2026, according to Empower Personal Dashboard data (2).

Simply put, half of all Americans in their 60s have at least half a million in retirement savings.

Millions of Americans are also set for a seven-figure retirement. Nearly 1 in 5 people (21.9%) have at least $1 million in their 401(k) plans, according to Empower (3).

In other words, the millionaire club might not be as exclusive as you might think.

However, if you're currently heading for retirement with less than $500,000 saved up, the good news is you don't have to start panicking yet. There are a few ways to speed up your progress.

While the half-million and millionaire club continues to expand, millions of other Americans are heading for retirement with far less capital. In fact, roughly 1 in 5 Americans over the age of 50 have no retirement savings, according to an AARP survey (4).

If you're part of that group, it might seem daunting to have to start building a retirement portfolio in your 50s. But you don't necessarily have to make big moves to get started. Even small amounts can grow over time with the right strategy in place.

articles.title: India Has Ideas. Now comes the test of impact
articles.summary: India Business News: What will it take to build a stronger, more inclusive and sustainable India, with technology and opportunity reaching more people?The answers will not.
articles.body: What will it take to build a stronger, more inclusive and sustainable India, with technology and opportunity reaching more people?The answers will not come from a single institution, sector or policy. They will emerge from the ideas India chooses to nurture today - in classrooms and laboratories, startups and enterprises, communities and homes.That is the belief behind TOI Ideas for India, a nationwide platform by The Times of India in partnership with Optum India, built to carry the country’s most promising ideas beyond conversation and into action.In its second edition, the response has been emphatic.The 2026 Innovation Challenge has received more than 14,000 registrations from across the country, from entrepreneurs, students, professionals, researchers, innovators and changemakers proposing solutions to the challenges and opportunities that will define India’s next chapter.Registrations may now be closed. But the real test is only beginning.Where the ideas are aimedSeason 2 is built around three themes that reflect the forces likely to shape India’s next chapter.Sovereign technology for India looks at how AI, cybersecurity, advanced manufacturing and home-grown technologies can strengthen India’s economic and strategic foundations, while creating solutions designed for the country’s unique needs.Inclusive innovation for Bharat asks how innovation can expand opportunity and participation - strengthening financial inclusion, widening access and enabling communities to become active participants in India’s growth story.Sustainable and resilient India focuses on the challenges that accompany rapid development, seeking solutions around clean energy, climate resilience, sustainable infrastructure, resource efficiency and circular models of growth.The themes differ. The underlying question does not.Can an idea solve a real problem - and can it do so at scale?That distinction sits at the heart of TOI Ideas for India. The platform is not looking for ideas that are merely new. It is looking for ideas that are purposeful, relevant, feasible and capable of creating lasting impact.As Uma Ratnam Krishnan, Managing Director, Optum India, says:“India’s greatest advantage is not just its scale, talent or economic momentum. It is the imagination and ingenuity of its citizens. The ideas that shape our future can emerge from anywhere, from a student, entrepreneur, researcher, healthcare professional or changemaker who sees a challenge differently and dares to reimagine what is possible. Through The Times of India Ideas for India campaign presented by Optum India, we are creating a platform that brings these diverse perspectives into the national conversation and connects innovators with the visibility, collaboration and support needed to turn promising ideas into meaningful impact. India’s progress will be defined by how effectively we harness the collective creativity of its citizens and translate it into solutions that improve lives, strengthen communities and accelerate inclusive growth. As we look towards Viksit Bharat 2047, I encourage changemakers across the country to step forward, share their ideas and help shape the next chapter of India’s development journey.”Raising the bar on what makes an idea matterWith 14,000-plus registrations, participation is only the beginning. The challenge now is to identify the ideas with the strongest potential to move from concept to implementation.For Ideas For India 2026, Grant Thornton Bharat has joined as Knowledge Partner, bringing expertise and rigour to the evaluation process.The partnership reflects a fundamental principle: meaningful innovation must stand up to scrutiny. Beyond the originality of an idea lies the harder question of whether it understands the problem, addresses a genuine need, can be implemented effectively and can create sustainable value.Vishesh Chandiok, CEO, Grant Thornton Bharat, says:“India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation will not be defined by growth alone, but by how effectively we use innovation and sustainability to solve some of the most complex challenges facing India. As we move towards the vision of Viksit Bharat, emerging technologies such as AI, digital public infrastructure, and solutions enabling the energy transition create an unprecedented opportunity to transform livelihoods, strengthen inclusion and accelerate equitable development across the country. At Grant Thornton Bharat, we believe the most meaningful innovation is purposeful innovation — ideas that create long-term value for communities, businesses, and society together.”Evaluation now begins the work of separating ideas that are simply compelling from those that can become credible, scalable solutions.A stronger second chapterThe ambition of Ideas For India 2026 builds on the foundation established by the inaugural edition.Season 1 attracted more than 11,000 registrations, with participants responding to challenges across economic resilience, health and well-being, and environmental sustainability. Thirty finalists presented their solutions at the national summit at Taj Palace, New Delhi, before an influential gathering of policymakers, business leaders, experts and changemakers.Those ideas were brought into direct conversation with some of India’s most influential voices, including Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai, Dr Devi Shetty, Dr Indu Bhushan and Abhishek Singh, alongside Uma Ratnam Krishnan, Managing Director, Optum India.The strongest ideas from the first edition were captured in the Ideas for India compendium, ensuring the thinking generated through the platform extended well beyond the event itself.Season 2 raises that ambition - with wider participation, sharper themes and a more rigorous evaluation journey.The Road to October 2026The next milestone is the TOI Ideas for India 2026 Summit in October, where the shortlisted innovators and their solutions move from submissions to the national stage.The summit will bring together innovators, policymakers, business leaders and experts to examine the ideas and the larger questions behind them. The final jury will evaluate the shortlisted solutions, bringing the Season 2 journey to its defining moment.For the participants, it is an opportunity not merely to present an idea, but to subject it to a wider conversation — to hear questions from experts, engage with decision-makers and demonstrate why a solution deserves to move forward.For India, it offers something equally valuable: a window into how its citizens are thinking about the country’s future.Because the significance of 14,000-plus registrations lies beyond the number itself. It represents thousands of people willing to look at India’s challenges differently. Some ideas will reimagine technology. Others will rethink access and opportunity. Some will address the environmental pressures accompanying India’s growth. Others may identify problems that have not yet received the attention they deserve.Not every idea will become a solution. But every serious idea adds something to the national conversation, and the best ones have the potential to change it.India@2047 may still be more than two decades away. But the foundations of that India are being imagined today.The question is no longer whether India has ideas. It does, in abundance. The question is which of them can withstand the test of scrutiny, scale and impact - and help shape the India we want to see in 2047.The answer begins in October.This article is part of a Brand Initiative, Ideas for India, by TOI in partnership with Optum. articles.title: What Happens When Strong Uptrends Meet Bullish Sentiment?
articles.summary: Uptrending stocks with optimism from analysts tend to outperform over the next month
articles.body:
Is there anything prettier than a consistently uptrending stock price chart? I'm drawn to these types of charts. I've always thought a consistent uptrend is an indication of strong buying power for a stock. However, while I can tell you if a chart looks like a consistent, methodical trend, it's hard to define it using data, which is necessary to create an indicator. That's why, until now, I've never put numbers behind my theory.

I won't go into the details, but using moving averages over various time frames, I've created a ranking system for stocks with the most consistent uptrends and downtrends over the past three months. Using this ranking system, Docusign (DOCU) is one of the top uptrending stocks. That's a pretty chart, if I do say so myself. When I see a chart like this, I think, why would it stop now?

In this week's article, I'll test my theory with actual numbers and see if DOCU and other stocks like it are good bets, like my instincts have always led me to believe.

My Trend Indicator and Next-Month Returns

For this study, I went back to 2024 and picked the 18th of each month, which corresponds to the end of this week. I used my trend ranking system to find the 30 stocks in the strongest uptrends and the 30 in the most consistent downtrends. Then, I tracked how each group performed over the next month of trading. The table below summarizes the results.

My instincts look correct based on the average returns of the stocks. The top uptrending stocks averaged a return of 2.15% over the next month, while the most consistently downtrending stocks averaged a return of 1.57%. The other stocks averaged 1.84%, falling between the two groups.

However, I'm a bit disappointed that the uptrending stocks were no more likely to be positive or beat the S&P 500 Index (SPX) than other stocks. Instead, the edge came from the size of the winners. The positive trades among the uptrending stocks averaged about 12%, while those among other stocks averaged closer to 11%. In other words, the top-trending stocks did not necessarily win more often; they tended to win bigger when they did.

I added a layer of sentiment to strengthen the indicator. My contrarian mind expected uptrending stocks where pessimism was prominent to outperform other stocks. My thinking was that more pessimism meant more pent-up buying power that could propel the stock higher. When I look at the numbers, however, brokerage analysts tend to be correct on these stocks.

To measure sentiment, I gathered brokerage recommendation data from Zacks Research. I separated the uptrending stocks from my study into three groups based on the percentage of analysts who rated the stocks a "buy." Stocks for which at least 80% of analysts had a "buy" rating averaged a return of 2.61%. Stocks that analysts were most bearish on averaged a return of 1.72%. The stocks analysts were bullish on also had the highest percentage of positive returns, at 57%. And even though the percentage beating the SPX was just 50%, that was better than the other groups.

articles.title: How Kraft Heinz is keeping its legacy brands affordable for cost-conscious shoppers
articles.summary: For Kraft Heinz CEO Steve Cahillane, changes in the grocery marketplace demand a shift in strategy.
articles.body: Years of high inflation have strained household budgets across America, putting a spotlight on the rising costs of necessities such as gas and groceries. They have also contributed to a shift in how consumers perceive value at the supermarket. New research from McKinsey finds that Americans are increasingly turning away from name-brand foods to lower priced, private-label or store-brand products. For Kraft Heinz CEO Steve Cahillane, these changes in the marketplace demand a shift in strategy. “We can’t just rely on having a strong brand and saying that’s going to be enough,” he said in an interview on a tomato farm in Woodland, California, part of NBC’s “Business in America” initiative. “Consumers have only so many dollars available for their food budget in a month’s time, and so you have to earn the right to be in that basket each and every day.” In recent years, store brands have shed their traditional associations with lower quality ingredients and temporarily “trading down.” Today, 85% of consumers believe private-label grocery products are just as good or better than those from name brands, McKinsey reports. Kraft Heinz sells more than 200 brands, many of them household names such as Heinz ketchup, Kraft Mac & Cheese, Oscar Mayer meats, Capri Sun drinks, Miracle Whip spread, Velveeta, Philadelphia cream cheese and Kool-Aid. But this is a challenging time to be in the name-brand food business. Last year, Kraft Heinz’s net sales in North America were down about 5% from 2024. When Cahillane took the helm as CEO in January, he was tasked with turning the business around. One part of that strategy, he said, is deploying promotional discounts more strategically. “We’re working with our retail partners to make sure that at the beginning of the month, when consumers are really doing their big shops, that we’re out there with good offers across the board,” he said. Consumers in general tend to have more spending power at the beginning of the month when government benefits such as SNAP are distributed, paychecks arrive and monthly budgets reset. “Promotions can be an effective means by which to drive that initial purchase,” said Erin Lash, a senior director of consumer equity research at Morningstar. But promotions can also create a new challenge: getting shoppers to come back once the deal is gone. “Promotions can be kind of a slippery slope,” said Mark Mayer, associate professor of Marketing at Indiana University and a former Kraft Foods brand manager. If customers “only buy your product when they can get it for a deal,” then the promotion defeats its purpose, he said. Unlike store brands, a company like Kraft Heinz needs a pricing strategy that both appeals to shoppers and also protects the brand’s status. “In general, competing on price is not great for established brands,” said Alexander Chernev, professor of marketing at the Kellogg School at Northwestern University. Unless a company is specifically positioned from the outset as a discount brand, slashing prices can undermine a brand’s identity. This is especially true for legacy products like those in Kraft Heinz’s portfolio. It requires Kraft Heinz to pull off a difficult balancing act: Making its products more affordable without diminishing the value of its brands. Cahillane said that when it comes to pricing, Kraft Heinz is not lowering list prices across the board. Only where the economics make sense. “The biggest price drop, where we’re bringing prices down, is most certainly in our coffee business,” which is home to brands like Maxwell House and Gevalia. A drop in global coffee prices strengthens the economic case for price cuts. As of Wednesday, benchmark coffee futures were down 30% from a year ago. Kraft Heinz is also offering some of their products in smaller sizes. “This isn’t shrinkflation,” Cahillane said, “this is recognizing that if we’re selling a 32-ounce bottle of ketchup and that’s too much for a family… we have a smaller 8-ounce bottle at a very affordable price.” It’s a strategy that has also been utilized by other major packaged food companies, including PepsiCo, Campbells and Mondelez, as they look to offer shoppers lower-priced options. Ultimately, Kraft Heinz must give shoppers a reason to pay full price, Cahillane said. And quality is what will justify the premium. “Value is affordability, but it’s also delivering the product quality and the promise that you’re making to consumers,” he said. “If they buy your brand, they’ll be receiving a value that they’re willing to pay for.”

articles.title: Fed expected to raise interest rates for the first time since 2023
articles.summary: Trump appointee Kevin Warsh was expected to lower interest rates. He’s poised to raise them. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
The Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise its benchmark interest rate on Wednesday, marking a sharp turnaround for an economy increasingly shaped by the war in the Middle East.

Inflation has been above the Fed’s 2% target for almost half a decade and has worsened since the start of the war with Iran .

That’s leading officials on the central bank’s influential rate-setting committee toward the first rate hike since 2023, a move designed to cool spending and prevent inflation from becoming more entrenched.

Raising rates could also weaken an economy that is already showing signs of strain, pushing up the cost of borrowing for consumers and businesses. However, keeping rates steady could rock the bond market, sending the Treasury rates that influence mortgages dramatically higher and spooking the stock market.

Stocks were mixed shortly after the opening bell on Wednesday as traders await the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates.

The S&P 500 rose 0.3%. The Dow fell 40 points, or about 0.1%. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.45%. Traders will be waiting to see how the Fed decision and Chairman Kevin Warsh’s remarks this afternoon impact markets.

The major indexes are each down six of the past seven trading sessions. Stocks are under pressure as bond yields rise to multi-year highs and global oil prices continue to trade above $100 per barrel after breaching that mark last week for the first time since July.

Yields and oil were slightly lower on Wednesday, providing a boost to stocks. Elsewhere, the US dollar index rose 0.1%.

Investors and Federal Reserve watchers are now penciling in the first rate hike in three years on Wednesday.

Goldman Sachs, Piper Sandler and other banks that previously projected a hold have switched their call after last week’s hotter-than-expected inflation reports.

This would be the first rate hike under Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who was nominated by President Donald Trump. Trump has made no secret of his desire for not just slightly lower rates but dramatically lower rates.

Ironically, Trump’s own policies have helped create a situation where his handpicked Fed chair has no choice but to hike.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a fierce critic of Kevin Warsh, sounds like she almost feels bad for the Trump-appointed Federal Reserve chairman. “Donald Trump’s economic policies have backed Kevin Warsh into a corner,” Warren told CNN. The Massachusetts Democrat argued that Trump’s war with Iran and his volatile tariff policy have driven up inflation to the point that Warsh and his colleagues must consider action. “He’s going to have to make a decision whether to bow down to Donald Trump and not do anything on interest rates, or to say to Wall Street that he is committed to bringing inflation under control,” Warren said. Wall Street widely expects the Warsh-led Fed will deliver the first rate hike in three years on Wednesday. “Either way…it’s the American people who are paying the price,” Warren said, noting that rate hikes will be an “economic disaster” for families by making it more expensive to pay off credit card debt and get a mortgage. “There is no happy solution at this moment based on interest rates.” Warren has previously criticized Warsh as insufficiently independent from the White House, even describing the Fed chairman as Trump’s “sock puppet.” But now Warsh could be on the verge of delivering the opposite of the deep rate cuts that Trump has been demanding. Asked if a rate hike would change her perception of Warsh, Warren said: “It takes a long time, more than one action, to rebuild a reputation.”

President Donald Trump said his pick to replace former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell would be someone who wants to lower interest rates. The man he ended up selecting, though, is about to give Trump exactly what he isn’t looking for.

“If I think somebody’s going to keep the rates where they are or whatever, I’m not going to put them in. I’m going to put somebody that wants to cut rates,” Trump told reporters in January, shortly before announcing he was nominating Kevin Warsh to helm the US central bank.

Trump has praised Warsh and said he trusts his handling of the economy. Instead, Trump has shifted the blame to 11 of Warsh’s colleagues who vote on interest rate decisions, calling them “political.”

September’s monetary policy meeting is Warsh’s third since he was confirmed in May, which means Trump may need to bite his tongue so as not to give the impression that he is unhappy with his decision. If he doesn’t, however, it could rattle markets, which are already under fire with Treasury yields spiking as well as oil.

Wednesday’s retail sales report showed that part of the August increase reflects higher prices at the pump — since retail sales are adjusted for seasonal swings but not inflation.

However, even when excluding those purchases, retail sales were still up a robust 1.1% last month.

Sales at gas stations shot up 3.1% in August as the war in the Middle East intensified again, continuing to disrupting the global energy market.

Retail sales were up across most categories last month, except at home improvement retailers and department stores, which declined 0.2% and 0.8%, respectively. In addition to gas stations, sales were up the most for online retailers (2.6%), specialty shops (1.9%), electronics stores (1.6%) and food establishments (1.2%), which includes restaurants and bars.

America’s economic backbone isn’t cracking just yet.

Retail sales rose 1.2% in August from the prior month, the Commerce Department said Wednesday, up sharply from July’s 0.5% decline. That was well above the 0.7% increase economists predicted in a poll by data firm FactSet.

Retail spending has trended lower in recent months, and the weak July reading raised questions whether the mighty US consumer might finally be buckling under the weight of higher inflation, mounting consumer debt and persistent economic uncertainty.

It turns out that’s not quite the case, at least for now. And that’s good news for the US economy, considering consumer spending accounts for about two-thirds of growth. Retail spending, which doesn’t including purchases on services, makes up one-third of overall spending.

Resilient consumer spending also shows the Federal Reserve has some room to raise rates to tame inflation, without risking pushing the US economy over the edge with a potential hike.

Stock futures were higher Wednesday morning ahead of the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates, set to be announced at 2 p.m. ET.

S&P 500 futures rose 0.4%. Dow futures rose 160 points, or 0.3%. Futures tied to the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.6%.

Stocks are coming off a day in the red. The stock market has been in a mini slump, with the S&P 500 down about about 2.75% since hitting a record high on August 13.

The S&P 500 has dropped six out of the past seven trading sessions as rising oil prices and bond yields have weighed on the market.

Bond yields pulled back slightly on Wednesday after the 10-year yield on Tuesday closed around 5%, its highest level since 2007 .

Yields have climbed amid a bevy of concerns from elevated energy prices and expectations for higher borrowing costs, as well as rising corporate debt issuance and unchecked government spending.

Oil prices were slightly lower Wednesday after Brent crude on Tuesday settled at $108.75 per barrel, its highest closing level since May 19.

From the market’s perspective, the Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday is already locked in. Traders are pricing in a 92% chance that the Fed raises interest rates by a quarter point, according to CME FedWatch, a real-time forecasting tool.

If the Fed were to hold rates steady, it would come as a major surprise to markets – and could stoke volatility.

“Historically, the Fed has seldom deviated from rate decisions that markets have priced with such high conviction,” Vail Hartman, US rates strategist at BMO Capital Markets, said in a note. “Surprising with a hold would trigger a sharp rally in the front end of the curve and a sell-off in longer-dated Treasuries, [the] US dollar and risk assets.”

articles.title: US retail sales rebound sharply in August
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 16 (Reuters) - U.S. retail sales rebounded more than expected in August as households stepped up purchases of motor vehicles and stocked up...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Sept 16 (Reuters) - U.S. retail sales rebounded more than expected in August as households stepped up purchases of motor vehicles and ‌stocked up for the new school year, reinforcing the economy's resilience ‌even as consumers grow more anxious about high inflation.

Retail sales jumped 1.2% last month after a ​revised 0.5% drop in July, which was the first decline in nine months, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Wednesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast retail sales, which are mostly goods and are not adjusted for inflation, rebounding ‌0.8% after a previously reported ⁠0.6% drop in July. Estimates ranged from as low as a 0.2% gain to as high as a 1.1% increase.

Last ⁠month's increase also partially reflected higher gasoline prices, which lifted receipts at service stations.

Households have continued to spend despite stubbornly high inflation because of the oil price ​shock and ​supply chain strains from the U.S.-led war ​with Iran. Consumers have, however, ‌become more selective and are seeking lower-priced goods. Consumer sentiment deteriorated this month.

Spending is being supported by steady wage growth and recent stock market gains. Households are also saving less and tapping into their nest eggs. The strength in retail sales, together with elevated price pressures and a labor market that is ‌regaining its poise after wobbling through much ​of summer, further strengthens financial market expectations that ​the Federal Reserve will raise ​interest rates later on Wednesday.

Retail sales excluding automobiles, gasoline, building ‌materials and food services surged 1.4% ​last month after an ​unrevised 0.4% decline in July. Economists had forecast these so-called core retail sales, which correspond most closely with the consumer spending component of ​gross domestic product, rising ‌0.4%.

Economic growth estimates for the third quarter currently exceed a 2.0% annualized ​rate. The economy grew at a 1.5% pace last quarter.

Imagine checking a long-forgotten account and discovering it's worth multiple millions of dollars.

Sarah, who said she has homeschooling her children for 20 years, checked in on her employee benefits account from when she worked for a tech giant and made a life-changing discovery. That's when she called into The Ramsey Show (1) to ask for advice.

Sarah's account had gone from worth barely anything to roughly $18 million at its current market price, she told Dave Ramsey. Although she didn't reveal which company it was, some commenters speculated that it could be Nvidia, the tech giant that has surged tremendously during the AI boom.

Regardless of the source of this windfall — and Sarah wasn't sharing those details — this sudden multimillionaire said she had "no idea" what to do with her unexpected boon. Ramsey, as usual, offered some advice.

Diversify and withdraw in a tax-conscious way

To be sure, finding $18M in a dusty account is a huge win, but it also exposes a simple investing risk.

Having so much of your net worth tied up in a single stock is "scary and unwise," Ramsey said. He recommended that Sarah offload some of the shares and invest her money elsewhere. However, given the magnitude of the fortune, selling even a fraction of the account would likely push Sarah into the top tax bracket.

This makes for a tricky situation. Sarah needs to start liquidating her stocks for redistribution, but she needs to be mindful of how quickly she does so.

According to the Internal Revenue Service (2), the highest possible federal capital gains tax rate for someone in this bracket is typically 20% — although there are some exceptions.

Depending on where you live, you may also face state taxes on your capital gains from selling long-term investments. For Sarah, in Washington state (3), that's another 7%.

While Ramsey suggested speaking with an expert tax planner or investment advisor to minimize her tax bill, he was crystal clear on the urgency of the situation. He insisted that Sarah diversify away from a single stock as soon as possible.

articles.title: SK Hynix stock jumps as memory maker responds to report of potential deal with Intel

What happened: SK Hynix ( SKHY ) stock jumped 3% in premarket trading on Wednesday following a report that the memory maker is exploring a deal with Intel ( INTC ).

Rivals Micron ( MU ) and Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) also rose modestly. The broader chip complex, including Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), Sandisk ( SNDK ), and Western Digital ( WDC ), edged higher.

What's behind the move: The South Korean memory maker responded to a Reuters report that it is in talks with Intel about an agreement to manufacture memory silicon wafers in the US for the first time.

SK Hynix said it is "exploring various options to strengthen its global competitiveness, but no specific plans or arrangements have been finalized at this time."

"No decisions have been made regarding the two scenarios mentioned in the article," the company said in a statement released on Wednesday.

What else you need to know: The media report, citing three people familiar with the discussions, claimed that as part of the deal, SK Hynix could lease part of Intel's Ohio facility, which has been in the works for years.

Another scenario mentioned was the establishment of a joint venture among SK Hynix, Intel, and major cloud companies.

The report also flagged possible opposition from Seoul as a major hurdle.

The US has been pushing to onshore advanced semiconductor manufacturing. The goal is to reduce reliance on foreign supply chains, which currently come primarily from Taiwan and South Korea.

Currently, Micron is the only one among the world's largest memory makers to produce its silicon wafers in the US. Its rivals SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics have invested in the US in areas such as packaging, R&D, and processors.

The tension for anyone holding TLT as a rate-cut bet is that the price of long money has kept rising while policy has stood still. Persistent inflation of roughly 3% gives the market reason to demand more term premium rather than less, which is a different problem than a Fed that eventually pivots.

articles.title: Amalie Lundstad, ingeniera, trabaja en una plataforma petrolífera con 250 días libres y un sueldo de seis cifras: "No es para todo el mundo"
articles.standfirst: Sus turnos durante dos semanas, duran doce horas y se desplaza en helicóptero
articles.summary: La
articles.body: Un trabajo con un sueldo de seis cifras, alrededor de 100.000 euros anuales, y con 250 días de vacaciones al año suena bien. El problema es que el empleo implica no salir de la plataforma petrolífera. Es el caso de la ingeniera Amalie Lundstad, que compartió con 29 años su experiencia laboral. "Este trabajo no es para todo el mundo, pero para quienes les gusta viajar y desean una carrera profesional apasionante, es un trabajo fantástico", explicó en declaraciones al diario sueco Expressen. Su historia ha vuelto a ser noticia hace pocos días ya que, a los 32 años, ha compartido en redes sociales su boda. La seguridad es la prioridad en las instalaciones. Por eso, siempre se trabaja en parejas: "Una persona se asegura de que el trabajo de la otra esté bien hecho. Si la situación se vuelve demasiado estresante, paramos y nos tomamos un respiro para planificar adecuadamente". El estrés puede ser un enemigo fatal en este tipo de trabajo. Y más en una jornada larga, de doce horas de duración. Los turnos de Amalie Lundstad duran dos semanas y viaja a la plataforma en helicóptero. Su salud siempre está controlada antes de los desplazamientos, ya que en la plataforma petrolífera es clave llegar sin problemas. La jornada arranca a las 5:45 o a las 17:45, en función del turno laboral que le corresponda. Es ingeniera de procesos y su trabajo está centrado ampliamente en la seguridad de la plataforma petrolífera. Amalie Lundstad también tiene una gran presencia en las redes sociales y recientemente ha compartido que se casa: "De estar con casco en el extranjero con turnos de doce horas a probarme vestidos de novia unos días después. A veces siento seriamente que estoy viviendo múltiples vidas completamente diferentes a la vez. Y ahora mismo el contraste es extra grande porque en dos días (el mensaje fue publicado hace cinco) me caso. Tal vez eso es exactamente lo que más me gusta también. Que mi vida nunca es solo una cosa".
